0600600600601f7.why: Stands in the chapter-number slot of the citation formula, written as four strokes, one mark, four strokes. The formula is proved: Matthew five strokes gives the salt and the light (Mt 5:13-14) at 108r, Luke seven strokes gives the widow's son at Naim (Lk 7:14) at 164v. But this sign's five occurrences lead to FOUR different chapters -- 195v to Peter and the keys and the third day (Mt 16), 134r to the king taking account of his servants (Mt 18), 202v to the tribute to Caesar (Mt 22), 071r to the lowest place at the supper (Lk 14). One sign cannot be four chapters, so it is not a chapter number and no arithmetic on the strokes (4+4, 4x4, 4-ten-4) survives all four. Left dark. Either the transcription normalises stroke counts, or the strokes are line filler beside the illustrations these folios carry.
